findings.title: Runner's concurrency machinery has no load test with latency/resource bounds
findings.description: The slice introduces real concurrency/process-boundary machinery: `RunnerTenant.tick` spends a single per-tick `TickBudget` across every project (with carry-over), `RunObserver` polls in-flight runs on an interval, `LaunchTracker.reap` polls/reaps detached `Popen` children every tick, and `probe_link`/`LinkProbes` spawn `cf` subprocesses. Per the Python rules, "any code on the … concurrency … paths requires at least one load test exercising a realistic configuration" that "assert on latency, throughput, or resource bounds," and "CI must gate load tests for slices touching these paths." The existing `tests/load/` tests do not exercise this: `test_crash_loop.py` drives `host_harness.start_host` with a throwaway `JOURNALING_TENANT` (no Runner), and the feed/inbox load tests that use `run_with_kills` start the real CLI (which now registers the Runner) but with no in-flight runs or CF links, so the Runner idles. The hot path — polling many in-flight runs, budget exhaustion across projects, child reaping — is only covered by functional/integration tests (`tests/runner/test_crash_recovery.py`, `test_end_to_end.py`) with no load bounds. A reasonable load test for slice 122 would drive the Runner against the stub `sq` with many `sq_run` entries and/or many CF links and assert tick latency, that no subprocess call begins after the deadline under load, and that reaped/leaked child handles stay bounded. (Partial deferral to slice 125 is defensible since `PRODUCTION_PLANNERS` is empty until then, but the observe/poll/budget/reap path is live now and is exactly what the rule targets.)

findings.title: `raise_expected_faults` takes a write lock for already-open fault kinds
findings.description:
`raise_expected_faults` calls `store.raise_project_escalation` unconditionally for every fault, then separately tracks `wrote`. For a kind that is already open, the store performs a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` + `SELECT` and returns the existing row without inserting (its documented no-op). In the common recurring case (e.g. `sq` down → `RUN_OBSERVATION_FAILED` every tick per in-flight run), this is a per-tick immediate write-lock per already-open fault kind even though nothing changes. A `continue` when `fault.kind.value in already_open` (before the store call) would skip the redundant transaction and also simplify the `wrote` bookkeeping to `wrote = True` on the actual write. Minor, single-process, but it's wasted work on a per-tick hot path and the design comment itself calls out the "writes nothing" behavior.

I verified the load-test claim against `tests/load/*` and `tests/host_harness.py`/`load_harness.py` (only `run_with_kills`→`start_background` reaches the Runner, and only idle), and confirmed the redundant-lock behavior in `src/amoeba/store/project_escalations.py:raise_project_escalation`. No FAIL-level or correctness issues were found.
